title: Minimally-invasive sampling of pars petrosa for ancient DNA extraction
author: Eleftheria Orfanou
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bqd8ms9w

steps.title: Prepare Workstation
steps.instruction: Set up a clean workspace to avoid cross-contamination.

substeps.instruction: Place a sheet of aluminium foil under the hood.
Place weighing paper, drill bits, and forceps on aluminium foil on a clean surface outside the hood (or inside the hood, covered with aluminium foil or paper towels).

Gather necessary materials: 2 ml Safe-Lock Biopur tubes, weighing trays/pans, labelled sample bags, small pieces of aluminium foil, tape strips, paper towels, diluted commercial bleach solution (1:10), and UV-irradiated filtered/deionised water.

steps.title: UV-Irradiate Bone Samples
steps.instruction: Decontaminate the pars petrosa using UV radiation.

substeps.instruction: Place a sheet of aluminium foil in the UV chamber.
Place the pars petrosa on the foil and place the labelled sample bag next to it.
UV-irradiate the bone for 00:15:00 on each side, using precision forceps to handle bones individually to avoid direct touch.
If irradiating multiple bones, ensure each is on a separate piece of foil with its corresponding labelled bag.

steps.title: Prepare Collection Tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare and label tubes for bone powder collection.

substeps.instruction: Label a new 2 ml tube and a new sample bag with the sample ID.
If starting a new session, tare the precision scale with the tube placed in the center.
Keep tubes closed except when adding bone powder.

steps.title: Clean Bone Surface
steps.instruction: Remove surface contaminants from the bone.

substeps.instruction: Remove the bone from the UV chamber using a paper towel dampened with household bleach solution.
Wipe the target sampling region with a bleach-dampened paper towel.
Clean the bone with a water-dampened paper towel to remove excess bleach.
Wipe the bone dry with a new sheet of paper towel.
Ensure residual soil is brushed or shaken off before starting.

steps.title: Set Up Weighing Area
steps.instruction: Prepare the collection surface for the bone powder.

substeps.instruction: Using a new pair of gloves, take a weighing tray.
Crease a sheet of weighing paper mid-way and place it under the sampling area to facilitate powder transfer.

steps.title: Identify Sampling Target
steps.instruction: Locate the dense parts of the petrous bone around the cochlea.

substeps.instruction: Target area c (located roughly halfway between the jugular fossa and the petrous crest).
Orient the bone to view the posterior part containing the internal acoustic opening (meatus acusticus internus).
Position the drill a few millimetres laterally and choose an angle parallel to the auditory canal to avoid penetrating it.

steps.title: Protect Bone Surface
steps.instruction: Prevent surface dust from contaminating the drilled powder.

substeps.instruction: Wrap the sample with aluminium foil and/or tape, leaving only the drilling window unwrapped.
Mark the position of the internal auditory meatus with a permanent marker.

steps.title: Abrade Sample Window
steps.instruction: Clean the surface of the sampling window.

substeps.instruction: Use the drill at low speed to abrade the surface of the sample window.
Discard or set aside the powder from this cleaning step.
Place a new weighing tray and/or weighing paper under the sample.

steps.title: Drill and Collect Powder
steps.instruction: Extract bone powder from the cochlear region.

substeps.instruction: Drill at low speed and high torque from the outside towards the cochlear region, parallel to the auditory canal.
Collect clean bone powder on the weighing paper.
If the drill enters soil-filled internal canals, stop and reorient the drilling angle.
Empty the drilling hole by tipping it onto the collection paper.
If soil is mixed with powder, separate them by repeatedly tipping the edges of the weighing paper; discard the dirt.

steps.title: Transfer and Store Powder
steps.instruction: Secure the collected powder in a storage tube.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the clean powder into the labelled 2 ml Safe-Lock Biopur tube using the folded weighing paper.
Close the tube, wipe it with a damp paper towel, and weigh it.
If powder is statically charged, use an anti-static gun on the weighing paper and tube.
Aim to collect 30 mg to 50 mg of powder; store any excess over 50 mg in a separate backup tube.
Record the weight in mg on the cap and side of the tube.
Store the bone powder at -20 °C.

steps.title: Post-Sampling Documentation
steps.instruction: Document the process and store the bone.

substeps.instruction: Take photos of the sampled bone for documentation.
Place the bone back into a new, UV-irradiated, labelled bag.

steps.title: Decontaminate Workstation
steps.instruction: Clean all equipment and surfaces to prevent cross-contamination.

substeps.instruction: Discard disposable materials such as aluminium foil and weighing trays/pans.
Clean surfaces and pliers with bleach solution.
Use less aggressive DNA decontamination reagents (e.g., DNA away) for electronic devices like the drill handpiece and precision balance.
Wipe bleach off with water-wet paper towels and air dry to prevent corrosion.
Incubate drill bits in a 1:10 bleach solution for at least 2 minutes.
Use a UV-irradiated and bleached toothbrush to brush the saw blade.
Clean with UV-irradiated water to remove bleach and let dry.
Replace drill bits after approximately 5 uses.
